verdict: Caution on Lucknow residential developers: lend only to RERA-registered local builders with completed phases and escrow-backed receivables; avoid first-time premium high-rise developers and pure land-bank plays.
title: Lucknow residential real estate: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Lucknow developer buys land, gets RERA and local approvals, builds towers, and sells units off-plan; cash comes in as booking advances and construction-linked instalments, and goes out as land cost, contractor bills and approvals. **The cash cycle is the whole credit story: money arrives before the building is finished, so the developer is effectively funded by buyers, not by us.** Value sits in the land and the approval, not the concrete. Pricing power is thin outside premium pockets, so margin is made on land cost and speed, not on price. Capex is lumpy per tower; a G+35 tower is a multi-year commitment. Where a figure is missing, collect from customer.

## What has changed in Lucknow now
Local news is narrow but clear: Emaar has launched 'Elara', a 194-unit, G+35 3BHK project at Emaar Gomti Greens, Sector 7, Gomti Nagar Extension, with prices starting from Rs 2.15 crore [2][3]. **That is a premium, branded, high-rise product testing demand in one corridor, not evidence of a city-wide upcycle.** The sources say little about Lucknow volumes, absorption or prices beyond this launch, so lean on first principles and peers. Peer results are strong but from other cities: Brigade's Q2 profit rose 29% to Rs 219 crore with sales of Rs 1,827 crore [4], and it plans over 7 million sq ft of launches in H2 FY27 [6]. Rating reports are old: ICRA's PEPL note is dated September 30, 2025 [8] and the Sobha note September 30, 2024 [9]; treat them as background, not current Lucknow evidence.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue local Lucknow builders with a delivered phase, RERA registration and a mid-income product in established corridors.** Also pursue contractors and channel partners attached to branded launches like Elara [1][2] — they get paid on bookings. Avoid first-time developers attempting premium high-rise on borrowed land money, and avoid anyone whose only asset is a land parcel with no approvals. When a proposal lands, check RERA registration and the delivered-phase track record first; if the developer has never handed over a tower, ask for a co-promoter or a completion guarantee.

## How to grow safely
Structure against the receivables, not the land: escrow the project account, take assignment of booking receivables, and keep a DSRA. **Take every month: collection statement, RERA quarterly progress report, unsold inventory by unit, and contractor payment status.** If collections lag construction spend for two quarters, ask for a fresh sales audit before any enhancement.

## Early-warning signs
- Booking cancellations rising while launches continue -> freeze new limits.
- Contractor arrears or slow RERA progress -> ask for the construction schedule and funding gap.
- Reliance on one tower's pre-sales to fund the next -> demand separate project SPVs.
watch: Collections below spend for two months -> ask for sales audit and stop enhancement
Progress behind schedule -> seek revised completion plan and escrow top-up
Cancellations rising -> freeze new limits and review receivables
Arrears reported -> ask for funding gap and co-promoter support
